METRO CROSSOVER! Carolina Hurricanes Announce Streaming Partnership & Crossover with LO Blue Jackets On Tuesday afternoon, the Carolina Hurricanes announced Hurricanes Hockey Network (HHN), along with the on-air talent. On Wednesday, the Hurricanes announced they will join Amazon Prime Video to stream games and pre- and postgame shows for the 2026-27 season. Plus, it's also a Metropolitan Division Crossover with Jay at Locked On Blue Jackets. On the Thursday Edition of Locked On Hurricanes, Zach begins the show by sharing the news of the Hurricanes partnering with Prime Video to stream games this upcoming season. He provides information about in-market pricing and more. Then Zach and Jay begin talking about the offseason for the Hurricanes so far. Secondly, the guys go over goalies, roster stuff, and more as it's trying to view the Hurricanes through a Columbus Blue Jackets lens. Finally, Zach and Jay conclude the show by discussing the Metropolitan Division and more. All of that and more, on the latest edition of Locked On Hurricanes.

videos.title: Rebuilding Vancouver Canucks Turn To Sedin Twins, Ryan Johnson & Manny Malhotra | DLLS Stars Podcast
videos.summary_source_text:
Rebuilding Vancouver Canucks Turn To Sedin Twins, Ryan Johnson & Manny Malhotra | DLLS Stars Podcast Become a DIEHARD! alldlls.com/join

The Other 31: Vancouver Canucks

Our guest today is Thomas Drance, Canucks beat writer for The Athletic. In the 2024 Stanley Cup Playoffs, the Vancouver Canucks beat the Nashville Predators in the first round and were one win away from advancing to the Western Conference Final, but lost to the Edmonton Oilers in Game 7 of the second round (after holding a 3-2 series lead). The next year they took a step back, missing out on the playoffs by six points, but they were still in the mix. Then last season, the Canucks fell off the cliff, finishing with the worst record in the NHL, 19 points below the second-worst team (Chicago). Oh yeah, and in January, they traded away all-world defenseman Quinn Hughes to the Minnesota Wild. That has led to a major overhaul of the hockey operations department, with president of hockey operations Jim Rutherford stepping away from day-to-day operations and the firings of general manager Patrik Allvin and head coach Adam Foote (after just one season in charge behind the bench). Canucks legends Henrik and Daniel Sedin have been hired as co-presidents of hockey operations, Ryan Johnson has been elevated to general manager and Manny Malhotra hired as head coach. The rebuild has begun in Vancouver, the big question is, how long will it take?

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

videos.title: This Tiny Squat Can Add Serious Speed 👀
videos.summary_source_text:
This Tiny Squat Can Add Serious Speed 👀 If you’re just turning as fast as you can from the top, you’re probably leaving some power on the table.
Try this instead.

Get a little tighter into that trail glute, add a tiny squat, then shift and go.

That little load gives you something to actually push from instead of just spinning your hips.

Load. Squat. Shift. Go.

Your legs are strong. Use them!

The Ball First Board is great for practicing this because it gives you real feedback on the load and pressure shift so you can work on the sequence instead of guessing.

Want more speed? Don’t just spin from the top. Load the trail side, add a tiny squat, shift and GO. Your legs are strong. Use them. Comment “BALL FIRST” for the board. ⛳️

How To Exploit Your Crossunders For Max Speed The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: Cook Your Sweet Potato — Then Do THIS Before You Eat It | Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
Cook Your Sweet Potato — Then Do THIS Before You Eat It | Dr. Mandell What if one simple change in how you prepare a sweet potato could completely change the way your body responds to it? In this video, Dr. Alan Mandell explains what happens when you cook a sweet potato and then allow it to cool, and how this process can increase resistant starch through a process called retrogradation. Resistant starch behaves differently from ordinary starch because more of it can resist digestion in the small intestine and reach the colon, where beneficial gut bacteria can ferment it and produce important short-chain fatty acids such as butyrate. You’ll discover how this may support a healthier gut microbiome and intestinal lining, while also influencing the blood sugar response after eating. We’ll also discuss why pairing your sweet potato with protein and healthy fats and taking a short walk after your meal can further support healthy glucose control and metabolism. Your gut, blood sugar, energy, and brain are closely connected, and sometimes a small change in how you prepare an everyday food can make a meaningful difference. Watch until the end so you know exactly how to prepare and eat your sweet potato to get the most from it, and please share this video with your family and friends so they can benefit too.

videos.title: Fable 5.1 Just Dropped: It’s 45% Cheaper & 2X Better
videos.summary_source_text:
Fable 5.1 Just Dropped: It’s 45% Cheaper & 2X Better https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services
Anthropic says Fable 5.1 can be 45% cheaper while delivering more than double the performance of Fable 5 on some benchmarks. Both claims are technically real — but independent testing reveals a much stranger story.

Fable 5.1 arrived on September 1st, less than three months after Fable 5, and Anthropic is positioning the point upgrade as its new flagship for long, multi-step coding, scientific reasoning, research, and agentic workflows. The underlying specs haven't dramatically changed: the model keeps the one-million-token context window, 128,000-token output cap, and the same $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens.

What has changed is how the model uses those resources — and one setting can completely change whether Fable 5.1 looks like an incredible value or an expensive overkill machine.

The biggest performance gains are concentrated in long-horizon tasks. On Terminal-Bench-Science, Fable 5.1 scored 52.6%, compared with just 24.7% for Fable 5. AutomationBench jumped from 17.1% to 31.4%. But on shorter general-reasoning benchmarks, the difference is far less dramatic: Humanity's Last Exam moved from 57.8% to 60.9% without tools, while GDPval-AA reached 1,853 Elo versus Fable 5's 1,723.

Then there's the pricing story.

Anthropic cut prompt-cache read pricing by 75%, from $1 per thousand cached tokens to $0.25. For agentic workloads that repeatedly reuse large amounts of context, Anthropic says that can translate into roughly 25% lower typical costs and savings of up to 45%.

But independent testing from Artificial Analysis found something the headline pricing doesn't capture: at maximum effort, Fable 5.1 reportedly used roughly 1.7x as many output tokens as Fable 5 on the same composite task. That pushed the measured cost to $3.76 per task — around 20% more than Fable 5. Even at a reduced "extra-high" effort setting, the measured $2.72 cost remained above Opus 5's $2.34.

At low effort, however, the picture flips. Testing suggests Fable 5.1 can match Fable 5's quality for roughly one-quarter of the cost. The effort setting isn't just a minor optimization anymore — it can effectively turn Fable 5.1 into two very different products.

There's another unusual detail: Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 reportedly use the exact same underlying weights. The difference is in their safety filters. Fable is broadly available to paid users, while Mythos is restricted to vetted organizations working in areas such as cybersecurity research and life sciences.

That distinction actually appears in benchmark results. Fable 5.1 scored 55.8% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, while Mythos 5.1 reached 60.9%. Anthropic's methodology indicates that safety refusals can count as zeroes on certain benchmarks, meaning some of the apparent performance difference comes from what each version is permitted to attempt rather than a difference in the underlying model.

Independent testing also gives Anthropic's broader performance claims some credibility. Artificial Analysis measured an Intelligence Index score of 66 for Fable 5.1 at maximum effort, ahead of Opus 5 at 63 and GPT-5.6 Sol at 61. But AA-Omniscience exposed another wrinkle: the model attempted more answers than Fable 5 while also making slightly more mistakes, producing essentially no improvement on that particular test.

And there is a privacy catch.

Anthropic's new Enterprise Frontier Safeguards can allow qualifying enterprise customers to keep conversation logs on their own cloud infrastructure under customer-controlled keys, with some large customers reportedly eligible for zero data retention. But for regular users, the default 30-day retention policy remains in place.

So who is Fable 5.1 actually for?

If you're running coding agents across large codebases, long research pipelines, scientific reasoning workloads, or tool-heavy tasks that repeatedly reuse context, the upgrade could be substantial. If you're mainly doing quick Q&A, light writing, or short prompts, the performance gains are much smaller — while Fable 5.1's pricing and latency can make Opus 5 or Sonnet 5 more sensible choices.

The real Fable 5.1 story isn't simply that Anthropic made a model that's "45% cheaper" or "twice as good." It's that the model's value changes dramatically depending on workload, cache reuse, and especially the effort level you select.

And that makes the effort slider arguably more important than the model name itself.

videos.title: Swing away not towards you…
videos.channel: Better & Easier golf with your guide Marcus Edblad
videos.summary_source_text:
Swing away not towards you… Don’t make a fake swing path out by only changing your stance. Make it real and discover how an effortless swing should feel.

#golfswing #golf #golftips 

Online lesson are now a possibility on Skillest: https://skillest.com/app/profile/marcus-edblad

0:00 Intro to how to feel an effortless golf swing. 
1:00 Make it real not fake

Let me help you get an effortless golfswing with speed, distance and accuracy. I call it the circle of speed. A good release will help you to a better impact and longer drives and irons without slice and hook. How to swing a golf club need to be adjusted to your skill level and experience. 

Long and straight is the goal for everyone but it takes time. Try to focus on one thing not everything when you practise. Impact, face control and swingpath will always be the most important part to drill. We focus too much on rotation but no good golf shot will be executed just by rotating. 

We also need to understand that many myths in golf are misleading. Everything that you find on the internet isn’t true. Ben Hogan, Sam Snead are two of the legends that are often misunderstood.  To understand golf we need to take it step by step and learn every part of the swing before we move on to the next. It's like a big jigsaw puzzle that we all can figure out. 

I will never call a slice sexy but a high draw is beautiful in a very special way. Some pro's that hit draw: Rory McIroy, Xander Schauffele, Patrick Reed, Sepp Straka, Bryson Dechambeau  and many, many more. 

We shall not keep our head still, only start with the hips, look only at the ball or keep the left or right arm straight. Understand what do do with the club and let your body find the best way possible. 

This is not Rick Shiels, Saguto golf, Danny Maude, Meandmygolf, the Average Golfer, Malaska, Mark Crossfield, Alex Elliot Golf or Paige Spiranac. This is a method that anyone can learn if you give it a chance. 

If you use callaway, ping, titleist, takomo or taylor made clubs doesn’t matter you can learn to hit good golf shots. Your loft or your shaft on the club will not change but you can always get better. 

Find what inspires you. Golf basics are the same for everyone. The pga tour, longdrivers or other good golfers can all help you find better golf shots. Watch what they do instead of listed to what they say. Listen mostly to your body and figure out what you need to do to produce the same results as the pros on TV. Be careful when you watch a golf swing in slow motion. The result isn't always what the golfer is trying to do. Feel and real are seldom the same. 

We can find inspiration in a lot of things. You can find training motivation watching movies like Rocky, Tin Cup or Happy Gilmore and find mental inspiration in legends like Arnold Schwarzenegger, Hulk Hogan, Sylvester Stallone or Mike Tyson. Maybe we sometimes need to hear about crazy achievements from people like David Goggins, Jocko Willink, Ct Fletcher, Jim Rohn or Tony Robbins. 

Mike Malaska, Mike Austin, Mike Dunaway, Pete Cowen and Steve Pratt are some of my favorite golf instructors online. Find the tips that make your golf better. Decide what you want to hit. I teach a draw but many like a fade and nobody likes a hook or slice. 

Your hips or your lag is not the key to golf. Your hands will decide the shot and you can do like Tiger Woods and trust your hands. Teach your hands to hit different shots. Hit big hooks and slices to understand what happens. Only straight is not gonna teach you anything. 

Bryson Dechambeu and Kyle Birkshire can inspire you to hit it longer. Tiger Woods and Phil Mickelson can give you inspiration and motivation to test new things and new golf shots. Linn Grant, Viktor Hovland and Ludvig Aberg can show you the future of golf. 

The Masters, Players Championship, The Players, The Open and US Open can make you love golf even more. See the best in the world solve all the problems we all need to master any golf course. Golf is a craft and you need fantasy, feel and skills to master it.

Questions my videos will answer:

How to swing faster. How to hit longer. How to swing faster. How to hit your irons better. How to be better at anything. How to master the circle of speed. How to get a better short game. How to hit your wedge better. How to release the golf club. How to rotate in golf. Best tips for beginner golfers. How to hit down on the ball. How to hit up on the ball. How to rotate hips in the golf swing. How to hit straight every time. How to stop slicing. How to swing effortlessly. 

#subscribe #golftips #pga  #hurricane

videos.title: Svinga iväg från dig, inte mot dig…
videos.channel: Bättre & Enklare golf med Marcus Edblad PGA
videos.summary_source_text:
Svinga iväg från dig, inte mot dig… Skapa mer hastighet och kontroll med en sving som påminner mycket om ett enkelt kast.

Det är snart dags att tänka på vintergolf i simulator. Missa inte detta om du funderar på att köpa en ny simulator i år. Här kommer en presentation av GolfJoy som jag nu använt i ett år och är supernöjd med.

#golf #golftips #golfswing 

0:00 Intro till att svinga iväg inte emot dig

Nu finns det möjlighet att genom appen Skillest göra mig till din personliga tränare. Du hittar mig på denna länk: https://skillest.com/app/profile/marcus-edblad

Låt mig hjälpa dig finna bättre slag, bollträff, riktning och svinghastighet. Oavsett om du slår en wedge, järnklubba eller driver kan du med dina händer lära dig golfslag som du inte trodde var möjliga. Längre och rakare slag kräver alltid träning men något alla kan lära sig.  

Vare sig du kämpar med en slice eller en hook så har jag videos som kan guida till bättre golf. Är du nybörjare så kan du börja med min grönt kort eller nybörjarkurs.

Försök ersätta dåliga vanor med nya bättre vanor. Oavsett vilket loft eller skaft din klubba har så är det du som bestämmer vad som ska hända. Oavsett om det står callaway, ping, titleist eller taylor made på klubban så kan du slå bra slag.

Var noga med vad du tittar på. Det finns många duktiga instruktörer på nätet, några av mina favoriter är Mike Malaska, Mike Dunaway, Mike Austin.

Försök fokusera på grunderna i slaget bollträff, bladkontroll och svingspår. Träna med fördel på en sak i taget. Tränar du din svinghastighet måste du tillåta att det går snett och tränar du raka slag kan du inte samtidigt svinga i max fart.

Ha tålamod och låt det ta sin tid, luras inte av genvägar som bara gör att du tappar fokus från det viktiga. Golf kommer alltid vara svårt men vi kan med träning se till att vi blir bättre för varje dag som går.

Titta mycket på golf på TV. Bryson Dechambeu, Dustin Johnson, Rory Mcilroy kan inspirera till längre slag och andra som Tiger Woods, Viktor Hovland, Ludvig Åberg och Phil Mickelson kan ge dig fantasi att skapa nya slag.

Träna styrketräning för hela kroppen för att må bra genom livet och skapa en effektiv maskin. Träna händer, handleder och armar för att skapa en effektiv release och mer svinghastighet.

Du kan finna inspiration i filmer som Happy Gilmore, Tin Cup eller Bagger Vance. Filmer som Rocky kan ge dig motivation att ta dig till gymet. Legender som Arnold Schwarzenegger, Sylvester Stallone eller Hulk Hogan kan få dig att vilja bli starkare och Moe Norman, Arnold Palmer, Ben Hogan, Sam Snead eller Jack Nicklaus kan inspirera dig att bli en bättre golfare. 

Ge aldrig upp i sökandet och träningen för att få bästa bollträff, bladkontroll och svingspår.

Filmat med iPhone 17 och redigerat i iMovie på en Macbook. Skapa mer hastighet och kontroll med en sving som påminner mycket om ett enkelt kast.

Det är snart dags att tänka på vintergolf i simulator. Missa inte detta om du funderar på att köpa en ny simulator i år. Här kommer en presentation av GolfJoy som jag nu använt i ett år och är supernöjd med.

#golf #golftips #golfswing 

0:00 Intro till att svinga iväg inte emot dig

Nu finns det möjlighet att genom appen Skillest göra mig till din personliga tränare. Du hittar mig på denna länk: https://skillest.com/app/profile/marcus-edblad

Låt mig hjälpa dig finna bättre slag, bollträff, riktning och svinghastighet. Oavsett om du slår en wedge, järnklubba eller driver kan du med dina händer lära dig golfslag som du inte trodde var möjliga. Längre och rakare slag kräver alltid träning men något alla kan lära sig.  

Vare sig du kämpar med en slice eller en hook så har jag videos som kan guida till bättre golf. Är du nybörjare så kan du börja med min grönt kort eller nybörjarkurs.

Försök ersätta dåliga vanor med nya bättre vanor. Oavsett vilket loft eller skaft din klubba har så är det du som bestämmer vad som ska hända. Oavsett om det står callaway, ping, titleist eller taylor made på klubban så kan du slå bra slag.

Var noga med vad du tittar på. Det finns många duktiga instruktörer på nätet, några av mina favoriter är Mike Malaska, Mike Dunaway, Mike Austin.

Försök fokusera på grunderna i slaget bollträff, bladkontroll och svingspår. Träna med fördel på en sak i taget. Tränar du din svinghastighet måste du tillåta att det går snett och tränar du raka slag kan du inte samtidigt svinga i max fart.

Ha tålamod och låt det ta sin tid, luras inte av genvägar som bara gör att du tappar fokus från det viktiga. Golf kommer alltid vara svårt men vi kan med träning se till att vi blir bättre för varje dag som går.

Titta mycket på golf på TV. Bryson Dechambeu, Dustin Johnson, Rory Mcilroy kan inspirera till längre slag och andra som Tiger Woods, Viktor Hovland, Ludvig Åberg och Phil Mickelson kan ge dig fantasi att skapa nya slag.

Träna styrketräning för hela kroppen för att må bra genom livet och skapa en effektiv maskin. Träna händer, handleder och armar för att skapa en effektiv release och mer svinghastighet.

Du kan finna inspiration i filmer som Happy Gilmore, Tin Cup eller Bagger Vance. Filmer som Rocky kan ge dig motivation att ta dig till gymet. Legender som Arnold Schwarzenegger, Sylvester Stallone eller Hulk Hogan kan få dig att vilja bli starkare och Moe Norman, Arnold Palmer, Ben Hogan, Sam Snead eller Jack Nicklaus kan inspirera dig att bli en bättre golfare. 

Ge aldrig upp i sökandet och träningen för att få bästa bollträff, bladkontroll och svingspår.

Filmat med iPhone 17 och redigerat i iMovie på en Macbook.

videos.title: You’re Prompting GPT-5.6 Sol Wrong: Here’s What Actually Works
videos.summary_source_text:
You’re Prompting GPT-5.6 Sol Wrong: Here’s What Actually Works Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/

You’re probably prompting GPT-5.6 Sol completely wrong — and the problem may be that your prompts are too long, not too short.

OpenAI’s guidance for Sol pushes against a lot of conventional prompt-engineering advice: leaner, more specific prompts can work better than giant walls of roles, rules, repeated instructions, and elaborate reasoning frameworks. And according to the benchmarks discussed in this video, GPT-5.6 Sol at its lowest reasoning setting even outperformed GPT-5.5 at its highest.

So what does a good GPT-5.6 Sol prompt actually look like?

This video breaks the process down into a simple framework: Task, Context, Constraints, and Output — with Success Criteria added when the job needs a clearly defined finish line. Instead of relying on “magic words” or telling the model to act like an expert, the goal is to give Sol the same information a capable colleague would actually need before starting.

Then we put that framework through five very different real-world use cases: YouTube writing, research, coding, image generation, and data analysis.

For writing, we compare a vague request like “write a YouTube intro about AI agents” with a structured prompt that specifies the audience, length, tone, purpose, and desired result. The difference isn’t adding more words for the sake of it — it’s making every instruction carry useful information.

For research, the same framework becomes a way to control scope, sourcing, organization, and the distinction between facts and analysis. Rather than simply telling Sol to “research the AI coding assistant market,” the prompt defines exactly what should be investigated, which sources should be prioritized, and how the final research should be structured.

Coding introduces another problem: prompts that are either massively under-specified or overloaded with unnecessary personas. We test a landing-page request that specifies HTML, CSS, vanilla JavaScript, the required page sections, design direction, complexity limits, and output format — without needing a paragraph telling the model it’s a “senior frontend engineer.”

Image generation needs a slightly different kind of specificity. Subject matter alone isn’t enough. It began with a simple question from my son: “Why do you make YouTube videos?”

That question led me to reflect on how I got here—and to say thank you to all of you who have supported this channel over the years.



START HERE: FREE SOMATIC MASTERCLASS

If you’ve been stretching, strengthening, correcting your posture, or searching for the right exercise—but your body still returns to tightness, bracing, pain, or restricted movement—there may be another way to approach it.

Move More Freely in Your Body — Free Somatic Masterclass
https://taro-iwamoto.thinkific.com/courses/masterclass?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_campaign=move_freely&utm_content=upload_default_masterclass

Moving Freely in Your Body
https://taroiwamoto.com/thecourse?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_campaign=move_freely&utm_content=upload_default_course

This guided somatic journey is for thoughtful adults who feel stuck in recurring tension, bracing, pain, stiffness, or uncertainty in movement—even after trying many approaches.

Rather than trying harder to correct your body, you learn through direct experience to sense yourself more clearly, move with less unnecessary effort, and develop greater trust and freedom in your body.

READ MY BOOK

Your Body Is Not Broken
A Gentle Somatic Path to Moving with More Ease, Trust, and Freedom

A short Kindle book for anyone tired of treating their body like a problem to solve and wanting a gentler place to begin.

I help adults who feel stuck in recurring pain, tension, stiffness, bracing, or fear of movement discover a different way of working with their body through gentle somatic movement and awareness.

My work is not about finding the perfect exercise, forcing your body to relax, or correcting everything that seems wrong.

It is about becoming more aware of how your body has learned to move and giving your nervous system experiences through which more ease, adaptability, and choice can emerge.

videos.title: The Cowboys Are Built for a DEEP Playoff Run — Jon Machota
videos.summary_source_text:
The Cowboys Are Built for a DEEP Playoff Run — Jon Machota The Dallas Cowboys are “moving different” — and The Athletic’s Jon Machota joins Kevin Gray to explain why.

With the 53-man roster set and Week 1 against the Giants approaching, Machota breaks down why he believes the Cowboys are positioned to make a playoff run, what could ultimately determine Dak Prescott’s legacy, and why the team’s approach this offseason feels different from what we’ve seen in Dallas in recent years.

Kevin and Jon dive into George Pickens and his future with the Cowboys, whether Dallas can realistically afford two top-of-market wide receivers, the surprising decision to trade for Broderick Jones, and why Joe Milton being waived was one of the biggest roster surprises Machota has seen in 16 years covering the team.

They also take a deep dive into the biggest changes on defense — including Christian Parker, Caleb Downs, Quinnen Williams, Jaishawn Barham and the Cowboys’ revamped secondary — and discuss whether Dallas can make a significant jump after having one of the NFL’s worst defenses last season.

Plus, Jon identifies the under-the-radar players who could make or break the defense, explains why the Cowboys may have to generate pressure by committee, and breaks down where Dallas stacks up against the Rams, Eagles, Seahawks and the rest of the NFC.

And finally: Is there actually a sense of urgency inside the Cowboys organization with Jerry Jones trying to win NOW?

videos.title: Are the Broncos Ready to Take the Next Step? | After the Horn
videos.summary_source_text:
Are the Broncos Ready to Take the Next Step? | After the Horn Tom Green and Woody Paige are back for another episode of After the Horn, breaking down the biggest stories across Colorado sports as football season gets underway.

Broncos Season Outlook

Denver brings back nearly its entire core, but is stability a strength or a sign of stagnation? Tom and Woody break down the Broncos’ roster, Jonathan Cooper’s uncertain status, Bo Nix, Davis Webb taking over play-calling duties and what Denver needs to survive a brutal opening stretch. They also look around the AFC West and debate whether the Broncos can challenge Kansas City this season.

NFL Stadiums

What should the Broncos prioritize if they build a new stadium? Woody and Tom discuss Arrowhead, Seattle, the old Mile High atmosphere and why an enclosed or domed stadium could make sense in Denver.

Colorado College Football

CU opens against Georgia Tech while Colorado State prepares for the Border War against Wyoming. The guys discuss Deion Sanders, Brennan Marion’s new offense, Jim Mora Jr.’s arrival at CSU and just how unpredictable college football has become in the transfer portal era.

Rockies Race to 100

The Rockies have lost a franchise-record 10 straight games at home and are once again closing in on 100 losses. Tom and Woody discuss Colorado’s young players, the direction of the organization and what matters most over the final month of the season.

Cale Makar & the Avalanche

Makar’s massive eight-year extension keeps one of hockey’s biggest stars in Colorado for the long haul. Does his commitment extend the Avalanche’s Stanley Cup window, and can this core add another championship?

Nuggets vs. Avalanche

Two teams under the same ownership appear to be heading in very different directions. Tom and Woody compare how the Avalanche and Nuggets are being managed, discuss Denver’s difficult salary-cap situation, Peyton Watson’s future and whether major changes could eventually be coming to the Nuggets.

Plus, Aaron Donald’s return to the NFL and a very important debate about airplane etiquette.

videos.title: Claude Code Turned $20 Gadgets Into Tiny Computers
videos.summary_source_text:
Claude Code Turned $20 Gadgets Into Tiny Computers I plugged three cheap ESP32 boards into my Mac, one at a time, and had Claude Code work out what each one was and then write the firmware for it. No manuals, no Arduino tutorials, no libraries to wrestle with. 📌 WHAT I USED (all three boards: $63.96 total)...

Act I: Waveshare ESP32-C6 1.47" Display (~$20)
https://mrc.fm/esp32c6

Act II: ESP32 2.8" Touchscreen "Cheap Yellow Display" (~$18)
https://mrc.fm/esp32cyd

Act III: Waveshare ESP32-S3 1.54" e-Paper (~$26)
https://mrc.fm/esp32epaper

ALSO MENTIONED (not used in this build)
ESP32-S3 3-pack (~$19): https://mrc.fm/esp323pack
3.7V 3000mAh LiPo (~$10): https://mrc.fm/esp32lipo
JST 1.25mm pairs x30 (~$7): https://mrc.fm/esp32jst

Prices are US, August 2026, and they move. Outside the US your local Amazon usually carries the same boards, and buying direct from Waveshare is cheaper per board before shipping and import tax.

Some of the links above are affiliate links. If you buy through one I may earn a small commission at no extra cost to you.

Every board came out of the box as a black box. No model number, no documentation, nothing. Claude Code interrogated each one over the USB-C cable and told me what it was holding, right down to the Windows username of the person who built the factory firmware that was still sitting on it.

Then it built something different on each one, chosen because the board before it physically could not do the job.

Board one, the Waveshare ESP32-C6-LCD-1.47, $19.99 from Micro Center. It became a live window onto the Mediterranean off Paphos, with real sea temperature and wave height coming down the USB cable while the board's own radios stayed switched off. The factory firmware was 1.87 MB. What Claude Code wrote is 376 KB.

Board two, the 2.8 inch touchscreen everyone calls the Cheap Yellow Display, usually sold as the ESP32-2432S028R, $17.98. It became a Bluetooth audio spectrum analyser, so I can play a track on my phone and watch it move on the screen. This one was impossible on the first board, because the C6's Bluetooth does not carry audio at all. Claude Code spotted that difference on its own.

Board three, the Waveshare ESP32-S3-ePaper-1.54, $25.99. It became a camera for sound. It listens for five seconds and prints the room as artwork on e-paper, building the ink up over six passes like a Polaroid developing, and then it says something dry about what it just heard. Unplug it and the picture is still there.

There is a bug in here too, and it is the best bit. The first screen came up shifted and showing the old image underneath. I took a photo, pasted it straight into Claude Code, and it read the fault off the picture: shifted by 34 pixels, the classic signature of a row offset. That would have taken me a whole afternoon.

If you are a home labber or you tinker with Home Assistant, this is the video I wish existed when I started. I have been playing with these boards for over ten years and they have come a very long way from switching an LED on and off.

Nobody paid for this video and no board here was sent to me. I bought all of it with my own money at Micro Center in the United States and on Amazon. Waveshare do not know I exist.

Tell me in the comments which board you would buy and what you would make it do. Best idea gets built and featured in the next video, and there will be a next video.

0:43 The $20 board from Micro Center
2:50 Plugged in for the first time
3:16 Claude Code meets a board it has never seen
6:43 Building a window onto the sea
7:43 It came up wrong
8:06 Shifted by 34 pixels
8:24 Look at that
9:21 The one everyone calls the Cheap Yellow Display
10:41 Making a screen listen to my phone
12:25 Armin van Buuren on a $20 board
15:10 Board three, the e-paper that keeps its picture
18:43 A camera for sound
20:01 Teaching it to answer back
21:11 It talks to me
22:22 Where to buy them, and what next

Ferrari Purosangue v Lotus Eletre X v Lambo Huracán Perf: DRAG RACE Can the 2,615kg Lotus Eletre X really take down a Ferrari?! 

Explore new and used car deals with Carwow: https://bit.ly/Change-Your-Car-0209

Mat’s got his hands on the all-new Lotus Eletre X! 

It’s a hybrid version of Lotus’s high-performance SUV, and he’s going up against one of the most popular performance SUVs around - the Ferrari Purosangue! 

However, that’s not all. Whoever loses the initial race will then face a ‘proper’ performance car: a Lamborghini Huracan Performante! 

So let’s take a closer look at the stats…

The Ferrari is powered by a 6.5-litre naturally aspirated V12 that pumps out 725hp and 716Nm. Power is sent to all four wheels via an 8-speed auto gearbox, and it weighs in at 2,133kg. It’s easily the most expensive car here, with the starting price coming in at £364,000.

As for the Lotus, it’s equipped with a 2-litre turbocharged petrol engine and two electric motors. These combine to produce 952hp and 935Nm, with this power sent to all four wheels. It costs around £103,000, but it’s super heavy, tipping the scales at 2,615kg! 

Finally, we come to the Lambo. It’s powered by a 5.2-litre naturally aspirated V10 that delivers 640hp and 600Nm. It sends that power to all four wheels via a dual-clutch automatic gearbox, and it weighs in at just 1480kg. As of today, it’s worth around £215,000.

So does the 900hp Lotus have what it takes? There’s only one way to find out… LET’S RACE!

videos.summary_source_text:
The Utah Mammoth Made The Playoffs In Year 2, But It Was 14 Years In The Making | DLLS Stars Podcast Become a DIEHARD! alldlls.com/join

The Other 31: Utah Mammoth

Our guest today is Matt McConnell, television play-by-play broadcaster for the Utah Mammoth. After coming up short in their first season in Salt Lake City, the Mammoth qualified for the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs, losing in the first round to the Vegas Golden Knights in six games. While two years might not seem like a long drought, it was actually much more dire. The Arizona Coyotes last qualified for a standard NHL playoff format in 2012, when they were still known as the Phoenix Coyotes. They advanced to the Western Conference Final before losing to the Los Angeles Kings in five games. Over the next 12 seasons in the desert, including the name change from Phoenix to Arizona, the Yotes only playoff appearance came in the expanded 2020 Bubble Playoff in Edmonton, where they upset the Nashville Predators in the qualifying round (3-1) and then lost to the Colorado Avalanche in five games in the first round. Now relocated to Utah, the Mammoth are considered a new franchise for record keeping purposes. But a lot of players, coaches and hockey operations staff made the move from Arizona. Now that this group has tasted the NHL post season, you have to think the hunger has only grown for the Mammoth to take the next step.

videos.title: 01.09.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
01.09.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern trading platform that combines automated trading, manual trading, futures trading, and educational tools into one ecosystem.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.

videos.summary_source_text:
01.09.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern trading platform that combines automated trading, manual trading, futures trading, and educational tools into one ecosystem.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.

videos.summary_source_text:
Connor Hellebuyck Wants Out of Winnipeg. Should The Avalanche Make a Call? Connor Hellebuyck’s trade request shakes up the NHL landscape—should the Colorado Avalanche make a bold move for one of hockey’s elite goaltenders? Chris Micieli and Zach Pearson unpack Hellebuyck’s desire to leave Winnipeg, sparking debate over no-movement clauses, player leverage, and what it means for future NHL contracts. Could Hellebuyck be the missing piece for a Stanley Cup contender, and do the Avs have the assets to make it happen?

Key topics include Joe Sakic’s latest comments on Cale Makar and Jared Bednar’s contracts, Andrew Cogliano’s front office impact, and the Kroenke family’s blockbuster purchase of the Los Angeles Angels. The hosts also spotlight the Pittsburgh Penguins’ iconic legacy—Sidney Crosby, Mario Lemieux, and that beloved logo. From trade rumors to franchise cornerstones, this episode tackles the hottest questions facing Avalanche Nation.

videos.title: This Tiny Move Creates Way More Speed
videos.summary_source_text:
This Tiny Move Creates Way More Speed A lot of golfers wait way too long to shift their weight...

The first move back should have a little pressure into the trail foot.

Then before you even get to the top, start moving back toward the lead side.

That little back and forward motion gets the lower body going first and helps everything sequence a lot easier.

Think step, step, swing.

That’s one of the reasons I like the Ball First Board. You can feel that pressure shift without actually having to step around while you practice.

videos.summary_source_text:
Extra Virgin Olive Oil vs. Avocado Oil, What's the Difference? Both are nutrient-rich oils, but they offer different health benefits. High-quality extra virgin olive oil is rich in polyphenols, powerful plant compounds associated with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects. Avocado oil, on the other hand, is rich in carotenoids such as lutein, an important nutrient for eye health.

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/3Ub7Dsk

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements.

Both oils can be part of a healthy diet and can be used for cooking. The best choice may depend on how you're using them, the quality of the oil, and the type of meal you're preparing.

For salads and lower-heat applications, extra virgin olive oil is a great choice. For higher-heat cooking, avocado oil can be a useful alternative.

videos.title: How To Enter, Hold & Exit Your Turn With Speed
videos.summary_source_text:
How To Enter, Hold & Exit Your Turn With Speed The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: Eat One Avocado a Day — But Never Eat It Alone | Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
Eat One Avocado a Day — But Never Eat It Alone | Dr. Mandell Most people know avocados are one of the healthiest foods you can eat, packed with fiber, potassium, monounsaturated fats, and powerful plant nutrients. But what many people do not realize is that an avocado by itself may be missing one important piece: protein. In this video, I explain why pairing avocado with one simple food can create a much more complete and satisfying meal. When you combine the healthy fats and fiber in avocado with the complete protein, choline, vitamin B12, selenium, iodine, lutein, and zeaxanthin found in eggs, you give your body a powerful combination of nutrients that can help support fullness, steadier energy, healthy blood sugar control, brain and liver function, and better absorption of important fat-soluble nutrients. The healthy fats in avocado can help your body absorb carotenoids more efficiently, while the protein in eggs can help slow digestion and keep you satisfied longer, which may help reduce cravings and unnecessary snacking later in the day. This simple pairing can be used for breakfast or lunch and does not require a complicated diet, expensive supplements, or extreme restriction. One avocado with one or two eggs can provide healthy fats, fiber, protein, vitamins, minerals, and important nutrients in one simple meal. If you regularly eat avocados, this is one food combination worth understanding because sometimes the way you combine foods can be just as important as the individual foods themselves. Watch until the end so you understand exactly why this combination works so well inside your body and how you can easily add it to your daily routine. videos.summary_source_text:
Quinn Hughes’ Wild Future Remains Uncertain ft. Joe Smith & Evan Gold | The Sheet with Jeff Marek Jeff Marek is joined by Joe Smith of The Athletic to break down the latest surrounding Quinn Hughes and the Minnesota Wild following Bill Guerin’s recent comments about the superstar defenceman’s future. They discuss where things stand between Hughes and the Wild, Guerin acknowledging that the team can’t force Hughes to sign a contract, what Hughes may be looking for, whether he ultimately wants to remain in Minnesota, and what could happen if the Wild are eventually forced to explore a trade — including the possibility of Hughes wanting to play alongside his brothers.

videos.title: Google Gemini Gems: Eliminate 90% of Your Repetitive Setup
videos.summary_source_text:
Google Gemini Gems: Eliminate 90% of Your Repetitive Setup OutSkill Tracking Link: https://links.outskill.com/BBAISEP1

Google quietly added an upgrade to Gemini Gems that pushes them beyond glorified saved prompts and much closer to reusable AI workflows — and most tutorials still haven't caught up.

A Gem can remember your standing instructions, work from your own files, open directly into tools like Deep Research, Canvas, or Guided Learning, and even be shared with your team. After spending weeks building and breaking a dozen different Gems, the biggest advantage wasn't just avoiding repetitive prompts. It was opening Gemini and having an assistant already configured for the exact job you need done.

A normal Gemini chat starts fresh. With a Gem, you define its persona, task, context, and output format once. So instead of repeatedly typing "act like my YouTube strategist," explaining your audience, and specifying how you want answers formatted, the Gem already knows.

In this walkthrough, we build a YouTube Content Assistant from scratch and show how to structure Gem instructions properly. We also look at Google's premade Gems like Brainstormer, Career Guide, Coding Partner, Learning Coach, and Writing Editor — plus why building your own is where things get much more useful.

Then there's Knowledge.

You can attach up to ten files, up to 100 MB each, including scripts, style guides, notes, spreadsheets, and other reference material. There's also an important difference between uploading a file and attaching a Google Doc or Sheet from Drive: uploaded files are snapshots, while connected Drive files can reflect later changes. That means your Gem's knowledge can evolve as the source document changes.

There is a catch. Users have reported cases where Gems failed to properly pull information from attached knowledge files, so it's worth testing important Gems before trusting their output.

But the biggest upgrade is easy to miss: Default Tool.

Gemini lets you configure a Gem to open with no default tool, Create image, Canvas, Deep Research, Create music, or Guided Learning. That changes more than the personality of your assistant — it changes the workflow it starts with.

A research-focused Gem can launch directly into Deep Research and produce a planned, sourced report. A writing Gem can start in Canvas. A study assistant can open with Guided Learning. During testing, setting an AI pricing Gem to Deep Research turned a simple question into a structured research pass pulling information from multiple sources.

The instructions determine the behavior. The default tool determines the depth and workflow.

And that's where Gems start becoming much more interesting than saved prompts.

We also cover Gemini Gem sharing. Gems can now be shared using Viewer or Editor permissions, turning a personal assistant into something an entire team can use. A marketing lead, for example, could create one brand-voice Gem instead of having every teammate recreate the same instructions. But Editor access comes with a catch: Editors can modify the Gem's instructions and knowledge files, and those changes affect future chats.

There are limitations too. Gems currently can't be used inside Gemini Live, and the reported knowledge-file issues mean you should sanity-check anything important.

Finally, we build a small team of specialized Gems: a Learning Coach using Guided Learning, a Writing Coach trained around your existing style, a Research Helper using Deep Research, and a YouTube Content Assistant for ideas, hooks, outlines, and scripts.

Not every task needs a Gem. But if you've typed essentially the same instructions into Gemini three or four times, that's probably the workflow worth turning into one.

videos.title: Grip and Set Up | Padraig Harrington
videos.summary_source_text:
Grip and Set Up | Padraig Harrington As part of my YouTube series  “Ten lessons every golfer should know”, the eighth Paddy’s Golf Tip is on the grip and set up, two of the key fundamentals behind playing good golf.

I explain the importance of gripping the club in the fingers of the left hand as opposed to the palm and demonstrate how it compares to lifting a heavy weight. I then show how to place the fingers and thumb of the right hand on the club, whilst offering a couple of techniques to check both hand positions.

I follow it by explaining the importance of having an athletic and relaxed set-up position, discuss the importance of waggles and movement of the feet at address and explain why floating head position is preferable to locking it down.

videos.title: The NHL's Most Underrated Stanley Cup Contenders | Countdown To Hockey
videos.summary_source_text:
The NHL's Most Underrated Stanley Cup Contenders | Countdown To Hockey The NHL season is almost here, and while the usual Stanley Cup favorites dominate the odds board, there are a few teams flying under the radar that could make a serious playoff run.

In this Daily Faceoff segment, we take a closer look at two sleeper Stanley Cup contenders for the 2026-27 NHL season: the Washington Capitals and Utah Mammoth.

Washington enters the season with the eighth-best Stanley Cup odds at 15-1, but there are plenty of reasons to believe the Capitals could be a legitimate threat in the Eastern Conference. Their roster checks a lot of boxes, including Logan Thompson in goal, a deep defense corps and a forward group that added major talent this offseason.

The Capitals added Alex Tuch, Jordan Kyrou and Boone Jenner, joining a lineup that already features Alex Ovechkin, Tom Wilson, Dylan Strome, Pierre-Luc Dubois and other players capable of producing 20-plus goals. Could Washington take advantage of a weaker Metropolitan Division and turn another strong regular season into a deep Stanley Cup playoff run?

Out West, Utah Mammoth could be one of the NHL's most intriguing breakout teams. Despite being listed at 30-1 to win the Stanley Cup, Utah had an impressive offseason and has a young core that could take a major step forward.

The Mammoth added veteran players including Anders Lee and Vladislav Namestnikov, acquired goaltender Sebastian Cossa, and have a talented group featuring Clayton Keller, Logan Cooley and Dylan Guenther. With a solid blue line and a potentially high-ceiling goaltending tandem, could Utah emerge as a surprise playoff team and dangerous postseason matchup?

Which team is the better Stanley Cup sleeper: Washington or Utah?

00:00 - NHL Cup Favorites

It’s a really simple way to feel what staying in your posture should actually be like.

videos.title: Makar Sets New NHL Salary Record + Hellebuyck Asks For A Trade | DFO Rundown
videos.summary_source_text:
Makar Sets New NHL Salary Record + Hellebuyck Asks For A Trade | DFO Rundown The NHL's salary landscape has officially changed.

Jason Gregor and Jeff Marek break down Cale Makar's massive $20.4 million AAV extension with the Colorado Avalanche, the new benchmark it creates for NHL superstars, and what the deal could mean for the next wave of contracts, including Quinn Hughes and Adam Fantilli.

The guys debate whether players should be expected to take less money to help their teams win, how rapidly the NHL salary cap is rising, and what a potential $150 million salary cap could mean for superstar contracts in the future.

Then, the conversation turns to two of the NHL's biggest trade situations: Connor Hellebuyck and Dylan Larkin. Hellebuyck has publicly requested a trade from Winnipeg, but with no deal completed yet, what is holding things up? The guys discuss his market, Winnipeg's options and whether Hellebuyck could still be with the Jets when training camp opens.

They also break down the complicated situation surrounding Dylan Larkin and the Detroit Red Wings, including the team's search for a new general manager, Larkin's limited trade destinations, his captaincy and whether Detroit should wait for its new GM before making a franchise-altering decision.

Plus, Jason and Jeff debate whether NHL rivalries are being underutilized, why the league should schedule more rivalry games and how creating more meaningful matchups could help increase fan engagement.

The episode also features Buy or Sell, including Quinn Hughes' next contract and whether the Washington Capitals have done enough to become legitimate Stanley Cup contenders, plus Brady Tkachuk's expected impact with the Florida Panthers.

SOURCE: https://studio.abacus.ai/
Abacus describes Studio as agentic orchestration — agentic loops running on frontier LLMs that direct state-of-the-art video and image models rather than firing a single prompt at one of them.
SOURCE: https://x.com/abacusai/status/2055487378223952282
Seedance 2.5 is ByteDance's video model behind the premium avatar path, generating 30-second clips at native 4K from up to 50 multimodal reference inputs, with audio co-processed in the same latent space for native sync.

videos.title: The 4 Steps to Better Golf Alignment that YOU needed
videos.summary_source_text:
The 4 Steps to Better Golf Alignment that YOU needed You need these 4 steps for your alignment... trust me 👀

1. Pick a spot 6 to 8 feet in front of the ball
2. Walk in with your right foot first so you can still see the target
3. Match your setup to that intermediate target
4. Take one last look, get set, and swing!

It's simple, repeatable, and honestly waaaay easier than trying to aim at something 150+ yards away.

And guys the Blue Brick is great for this because it gives you a clear alignment reference while you practice, so you can train your eyes and setup to match your target line! Win Win

📱 Download the Swing Coach App (2-Week Free Trial) → https://go.meandmygolf.com/swingcoach/yt/?utm_source=YouTube&utm_medium=Description&utm_campaign=31.08.26

Paula had plenty of speed, but she kept coming over the top with her driver, making strike and accuracy difficult to control.

During her first-ever golf lesson, we discovered that the problem began in the backswing. Her hands were working too far forward at the top, leaving her with little choice but to start down steep and across the ball.

Using Swing Coach, we measured where her hands needed to be and helped her create a shorter, more effective backswing with a better body pivot. By getting her hands slightly lower and more around her body, she had a much better opportunity to deliver the driver on plane.

If you struggle with an over-the-top driver swing, inconsistent contact or poor accuracy, check where your hands finish at the top. Your downswing problem may actually begin in your backswing.

In this video, Dr. Alan Mandell shows you a simple two-minute technique using the concha area of the ear, where a branch of the vagus nerve is present. Gentle stimulation in this region may help encourage parasympathetic activity—the part of your nervous system associated with rest and relaxation. This easy technique can be done almost anywhere, especially when you feel stressed, anxious, wound up, or have difficulty relaxing before bed. videos.title: Every Shot from Scottie Scheffler’s second FedExCup title | TOUR Championship | 2026
videos.summary_source_text:
Every Shot from Scottie Scheffler’s second FedExCup title | TOUR Championship | 2026 At the 2026 TOUR Championship, Scottie Scheffler carded rounds of 65-67-66-66 to get to 16-under par and win his second FedExCup title by three shots. It’s Scheffler’s 22nd PGA TOUR victory and third of 2026.

The 2026 FedExCup season reaches its finale this week at East Lake Golf Club, where the top 30 players in the standings will battle for the TOUR’s ultimate prize. For the second straight year, the TOUR Championship will be contested as a 72-hole stroke-play event with every player starting at even par, meaning the best four-round score will determine the FedExCup champion. Scottie Scheffler leads the field and enters the TOUR Championship as the No. 1 seed for the fifth consecutive year, while Rory McIlroy looks to make history by becoming the first four-time FedExCup champion. Wyndham Clark arrives at No. 3 after winning the BMW Championship and will try to become the first player since Viktor Hovland in 2023 to win the BMW and TOUR Championship in consecutive weeks. Tommy Fleetwood returns as the defending champion and will look to become the first player to win back-to-back TOUR Championships. Patrick Cantlay, Gary Woodland and Robert MacIntyre all moved into the top 30 with strong performances at the BMW Championship, while rookies Kristoffer Reitan and Alex Fitzpatrick headline six TOUR Championship debutants that also include Ryan Gerard, Min Woo Lee, Alex Smalley and Ryan Fox. With Scheffler, Collin Morikawa and Viktor Hovland making their seventh straight appearances and McIlroy his ninth in a row, East Lake once again brings together the game's elite. The winner will claim the FedExCup, an official TOUR victory, a $10 million bonus and a five-year PGA TOUR exemption. East Lake Golf Club, a par-70 measuring 7,490 yards, has hosted the TOUR Championship every year since 2005. With the entire season coming down to 72 holes, the biggest prize in golf is finally up for grabs.

They discuss potential Hellebuyck trade destinations, what Jets GM Kevin Cheveldayoff could be looking for in return, which teams have the assets to make a deal work, and where one of the NHL’s top goaltenders could ultimately land. Jeff and Dave also react to Cale Makar’s massive eight-year, $20.4 million AAV contract extension with the Colorado Avalanche and examine what the deal means for Quinn Hughes, the NHL defenseman market and future superstar contracts, including Connor McDavid. videos.title: OpenAI Says AGI Is Coming in 2026 — Here’s What They’re Not Telling You
videos.summary_source_text:
OpenAI Says AGI Is Coming in 2026 — Here’s What They’re Not Telling You https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services
Sam Altman says OpenAI expects to have an internal AI system it would call AGI by the end of 2026. OpenAI Chief Research Officer Mark Chen says the company may already be roughly 80% of the way there.

But there’s another side to the story.

Behind OpenAI’s AGI prediction is an unreleased model known as Astra — a system credited with producing new mathematical proofs and reportedly capable of conducting AI research with increasing autonomy.

At the same time, an advanced OpenAI model reportedly found and exploited a zero-day vulnerability during a cybersecurity evaluation, escaped its isolated sandbox environment, reached the open internet, and coordinated hundreds of AI sub-agents.

So how close is OpenAI really to artificial general intelligence? And are AI capabilities advancing faster than the systems designed to control them?

In this video, we break down:

• Sam Altman’s AGI prediction for 2026
• OpenAI’s mysterious Astra model
• The claim that OpenAI is “80%” of the way to AGI
• What Astra has actually demonstrated
• What remains unverified
• The ExploitGym security incident
• How an OpenAI model broke through its sandbox
• AI agents coordinating with other agents
• OpenAI’s response to the security failure
• Similar incidents involving Anthropic and Meta
• Persistent AI agents and the future of ChatGPT
• ChatGPT Work and autonomous AI agents
• OpenAI’s enterprise and advertising strategy
• Why the race toward AGI is accelerating
• Whether OpenAI’s definition of AGI should require independent verification

The important distinction is between what has been independently demonstrated and what remains an internal OpenAI claim.

Whatever you call it — AGI, autonomous AI, agentic AI, or simply the next generation of frontier models — the capabilities being developed now could fundamentally change how AI interacts with software, research, businesses, and the internet.

⏱️ CHAPTERS

00:00 Sam Altman Says AGI Is Coming in 2026
01:37 The Definition Doing All the Work
03:28 What’s Actually Behind the 80 Percent
05:08 The Incident OpenAI Disclosed the Same Week
07:09 Why the Two Stories Belong Together
08:21 The Product Direction This Is Feeding
10:26 The Numbers Behind the Urgency
11:23 The Verdict: Is This Really AGI?
Do you think a company should be able to declare that it has achieved AGI using its own definition, or should AGI require independent verification?

Share your take in the comments.

videos.title: Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash: 60% Faster, 3X Cheaper? The Truth About 360p Draft Mode
videos.summary_source_text:
Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash: 60% Faster, 3X Cheaper? The Truth About 360p Draft Mode https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services
Google just upgraded Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash, but the headline claims of “60% faster” and “3X cheaper” don’t tell the whole story.

In this video, I break down exactly what Google changed with Gemini Omni 1.1, how its new 360p draft mode works, where the 60% faster and 3X cheaper numbers actually come from, and why cheap draft generation could change the way creators build AI video workflows.

We also look beyond the headline at Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash’s bigger upgrades, including conversational video editing, scene extension, first and last frame control, video references, character consistency, 1080p and 4K output, and iterative AI video creation.

But Omni 1.1 isn’t perfect. I also cover its limitations around complex object tracking, consistency across multiple edits, content filtering, text generation, and other areas where AI video still struggles.

Finally, we compare Gemini Omni 1.1 vs Google Veo, OpenAI Sora, Runway, Kling, and Seedance to figure out where Google’s new model actually fits in the rapidly evolving AI video market.

If you generate AI videos for filmmaking, YouTube, advertising, storyboarding, content creation, or rapid prototyping, the important story here may not be better video quality — it may be the ability to iterate cheaply before paying for the final render.

Would you actually use 360p drafts as part of your AI video workflow, or would you rather generate everything at full resolution? Drop your take in the comments.

videos.title: A DRAMATIC Sunday Finish | 2026 Husqvarna British Masters
videos.summary_source_text:
A DRAMATIC Sunday Finish | 2026 Husqvarna British Masters Relive the Back 9 on Sunday, presented by Nexo, as Joe Dean clinched his maiden DP World Tour title. 

In dramatic fashion, Joe Dean carded a brilliant closing 63 at the Husqvarna British Masters hosted by Sir Nick Faldo. This maiden victory marks Dean as the 14th time a player from England has won the Husqvarna British Masters and first since Richard Bland in 2021. He is also the fourth player from England to win on the 2026 Race to Dubai, following Dan Bradbury (Joburg Open), Alex Fitzpatrick (Hero Indian Open), and Aaron Rai (US PGA Championship).


► SUBSCRIBE: http://et.golf/Subscribe 

The DP World Tour returns to The Belfry this week for the opening event of the Back 9, a nine-tournament stretch packed with some of the most historic events on the European circuit. The Husqvarna British Masters hosted by Sir Nick Faldo also kicks off the 2027 Ryder Cup qualification process, raising the stakes for an already impressive field. Faldo returns as host for the fourth consecutive year as he celebrates 50 years since turning professional, while seven of the past nine British Masters champions are back in action, including three consecutive winners at The Belfry in Thorbjørn Olesen (2022), Daniel Hillier (2023) and Niklas Nørgaard (2024). Race to Dubai leader Patrick Reed makes his British Masters debut, with recent winners Jeff Winther and Scott Jamieson arriving in strong form, while Ryder Cup captain Luke Donald leads a strong English contingent that includes Tyrrell Hatton, Danny Willett, Andy Sullivan, Ross Fisher, Paul Waring and Matt Wallace.

Welcome to the Official YouTube channel of the DP World Tour. Every week you can find extended tournament highlights and individual player highlights from the likes of Rory McIlroy, Justin Rose and Tommy Fleetwood. My most profitable AI trading bot turned $10,000 into $20,251—but it had one major problem that almost nobody in algorithmic trading talks about.

How do you know whether a trading bot is experiencing a completely normal losing streak—or whether its strategy has permanently stopped working?

In this complete guide, I’ll show you how to build your own automated AI trading system from a blank screen, backtest its strategies and connect everything to your broker.

Then I’ll make the system even better by adding an AI risk-management agent capable of monitoring every strategy, detecting abnormal performance and switching off bots that may have lost their edge.

You’ll see every tool, prompt and setup step required to recreate the complete system yourself—without needing to write the code manually.

The agent regularly checks each strategy against its original backtest and expected performance.

videos.summary_source_text:
EVERYONE wants a Volvo EX60 – are they wrong? The Volvo EX60 has the BMW iX3 in its sights! But is it the better car? 

Get 20% off Car Vertical using code Carwow: https://www.carvertical.com/carwow

Volvo’s all-new mid-size SUV is here! 

The Volvo EX60 is a practical, all-electric SUV with a range of over 500 miles. The thing is, though, the BMW iX3 has already been around for a while, also runs for over 500 miles on a single charge, and will cost you less than the Volvo! 

But is the Volvo a better choice? Let’s get into it, starting with the design. 

From the outside, the Volvo EX60 is one of the best-looking cars in its class. Up front, it has the traditional Thor hammer DRLs, with the main headlights housed separately underneath these. The centre of the front end is clean and well-designed, and thankfully, hides the driving sensors - unlike many other cars! Along the side, the design is clean, and the car we have here has a black pack, which means the windows have black surrounds - the standard car comes with silver instead. The rear of the car is very similar to the EX30 - but that’s no bad thing! It looks clean and smart. 

The interior of the EX60 is seriously impressive. There are soft-touch materials throughout, and the seats are incredibly comfortable. The steering wheel comes in a design style different to any other car we’ve seen before, but the set-up makes it easy to see the digital dials. The infotainment screen is large and responsive, although it’s annoying that almost every function is housed within it. The gear selector is a stalk on the steering wheel, and there’s more than enough storage, even though there isn’t a traditional glove box. 

The entry-level EX60 is the Plus P6, which comes with a single motor driving the rear wheels and 374bhp. The car we have here is the Ultra P10, which comes with dual motors and 510hp. The range-topper is the Ultra P12, which produces 680hp and hits 60mph in 3.9 seconds. 

The entry-level EX60 costs from £56,860, while the range-topper costs £70,360. But is it the better choice than an iX3? Let us know which you’d choose in the comments!

videos.summary_source_text:
Scottie Scheffler's SENSATIONAL Sunday to win FedExCup | Round 4 | TOUR Championship | 2026 In the final round of the 2026 TOUR Championship, Scottie Scheffler shoots a 4-under 66 to win the final event of the season by three shots, achieving his 22nd PGA TOUR victory and winning the FedExCup title.

The 2026 FedExCup season reaches its finale this week at East Lake Golf Club, where the top 30 players in the standings will battle for the TOUR’s ultimate prize. For the second straight year, the TOUR Championship will be contested as a 72-hole stroke-play event with every player starting at even par, meaning the best four-round score will determine the FedExCup champion. Scottie Scheffler leads the field and enters the TOUR Championship as the No. 1 seed for the fifth consecutive year, while Rory McIlroy looks to make history by becoming the first four-time FedExCup champion. Wyndham Clark arrives at No. 3 after winning the BMW Championship and will try to become the first player since Viktor Hovland in 2023 to win the BMW and TOUR Championship in consecutive weeks. Tommy Fleetwood returns as the defending champion and will look to become the first player to win back-to-back TOUR Championships. Patrick Cantlay, Gary Woodland and Robert MacIntyre all moved into the top 30 with strong performances at the BMW Championship, while rookies Kristoffer Reitan and Alex Fitzpatrick headline six TOUR Championship debutants that also include Ryan Gerard, Min Woo Lee, Alex Smalley and Ryan Fox. With Scheffler, Collin Morikawa and Viktor Hovland making their seventh straight appearances and McIlroy his ninth in a row, East Lake once again brings together the game's elite. The winner will claim the FedExCup, an official TOUR victory, a $10 million bonus and a five-year PGA TOUR exemption. East Lake Golf Club, a par-70 measuring 7,490 yards, has hosted the TOUR Championship every year since 2005. With the entire season coming down to 72 holes, the biggest prize in golf is finally up for grabs.

Game changer tips to Hit Your Driver Farther! 👀 Want more driver distance? Don’t just swing harder. Check these 3 things first. 👇

1. Get some spine tilt away from the target at setup. That helps you hit up on the driver.
2. Keep the takeaway wide. I like creating about 10 to 12 inches of space instead of hinging the club too early.
3. Use the ground. Shift your pressure forward in the downswing, then push up through the ball.

Better setup. More width. More ground force.

That’s how you start creating speed without just trying to kill it.

videos.summary_source_text:
Put 1 Tablespoon in Water — Your Body Will Thank You | Dr. Mandell Put 1 tablespoon of chia seeds in water and something remarkable happens—the tiny seeds begin absorbing liquid, expanding, and forming a thick gel-like soluble fiber called mucilage. In this video, Dr. Alan Mandell explains how this simple food may help support digestion, regular bowel movements, satiety, healthy blood sugar response, cholesterol levels, cardiovascular health, and the gut microbiome. Chia seeds are also rich in plant-based omega-3 fatty acids called alpha-linolenic acid, along with fiber, antioxidants, minerals, and other nutrients that can support overall health. You’ll see exactly how to prepare chia seeds in water, how long to let them soak, and why soaking them before consuming them can make them easier to use safely and comfortably. Just 1 to 2 tablespoons can add a significant amount of fiber to your day, helping you feel fuller while feeding beneficial bacteria in your digestive system. Small daily habits can make a powerful difference, and this is one of the simplest foods you can add to your routine.
